topics.topic: Scope of token-protected project operations and authentication required outside that scope
questions: What exactly makes an operation “on a project,” and does “every operation” mean every deliverer operation or also the agent, calling flow and Portal actions described in these decisions?
May a deliverer operation that is classified as not being on a project be called without authentication, and which such operations, if any, are allowed?

Do writing a connection record, clearing its confirmation after a folder change, and recording the owner's renewed confirmation count as protected project operations, and if so who supplies the token when the agent performs them?
Does the agent's one-project-at-a-time date repair require this token in addition to the owner's permission, or is repair outside the operations governed by R0-15?

Which actions count as operations on a project, specifically deliver-one-photo, record-publication, and writing or changing an object's folder connection, and what authentication is required for actions outside that category?

quotes: The HTTP surface with the health, scan, delivery and mark routes.

None until the surface is served. The health route answers without a token. Every other route checks the token, the project id and the form of its body when it has one, calls one operation of `module:photo_delivery` and turns its refusal into an answer.

The calling agent is outside this service and organises the work (R0-15). It reads and publishes in the Portal with
its own session. It reaches the deliverer only through the authenticated routes of `module:deliverer_api`, which
delegates to `module:photo_delivery`. The deliverer never calls the Portal. Showing a photo to the client is a later
action of the owner in the Portal and is not part of this flow.

The agent writes the connection for a project the Registry already
issued, and sets the confirmation only for the folders the owner confirmed. When the agent later
changes the root or a subfolder it clears the confirmation in the same write, and sets it again
after the owner confirms the new folders (R0-11). `label` is a name for people, written by the
agent; changing it affects neither the identity nor the confirmation. The deliverer only reads the
connection.

The agent repairs the dates of one project at a time, after a backup and with the owner's
   permission for that project (R0-13). The repair changes the Portal's data, not the deliverer's.
judgement.why: States 1, 2, 4 and 5 limit the token-protected service surface to scan, delivery and mark routes, exempt only health, and place connection maintenance, Portal actions and date repair outside the deliverer.

topics.topic: Failure responses and state-safety guarantees for missing or invalid authorization
questions: What observable result must each operation return when the token is absent, malformed, expired, invalid or unauthorized for the project, and must it avoid reading or changing project state in every such case?

quotes:
Every operation except the health answer requires the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`,
   compared whole, case-sensitively and in constant time. Any other value is refused with 401 before
   the request's identifiers or body are examined.

A token is replaced by writing a new file and restarting the service. The old token then stops
   working. The token is never written to logs, answers, repository files or the manifest.

Each scan, placement and mark reads the connections file exactly once, at its connection check,
   and uses that reading for the whole operation. A change written later applies from the next
   operation without a restart, and an operation that has already read the file finishes on that
   reading. A request refused before its connection check does not read the file.

None until the surface is served. The health route answers without a token. Every other route checks the token, the project id and the form of its body when it has one, calls one operation of `module:photo_delivery` and turns its refusal into an answer.
judgement.why: State 2 requires every absent, malformed or incorrect bearer value to receive 401 before identifiers, bodies or connection state are examined, and token replacement makes the old value invalid; State 5 places that check before invoking the project operation.

topics.topic: Token identity, issuer, custody, and validator
questions: What token is this, who issues it, which actor obtains and stores it, and which system validates it?

topics.topic: Whether the token must authorize the specific project
questions: Does possession of the token merely authenticate the caller, or must the token authorize the particular project named or implied by the operation?

quotes: There is one principal: the calling flow of the owner. It may act on every confirmed connection.
judgement.why: State 2 makes the bearer credential service-wide for the owner's single calling-flow principal rather than project-specific.
